references.text: Moses gives instructions on how to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days, confirming the timing and duration of the feast mentioned in Leviticus.
Refers to the Feast of Tabernacles as a time for reading the Law aloud and links the festival to spiritual renewal.
Describes the sacrifices that are to be brought on the fifteenth day of the seventh month during the Feast of Tabernacles.
Ezra and the people celebrated the Feast of Tabernacles after returning from exile, in accordance with what is written in the Law.
Nehemiah describes the restoration of the Feast of Tabernacles through the building of booths, as prescribed in the Law of Moses.
The prophecy that all nations will come to Jerusalem to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles in the messianic age.
John mentions that the Jewish Feast of Tabernacles was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem in connection with this festival.
On the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus cried out about living water, linking the Feast of Tabernacles to spiritual fulfillment.
